Subject: Proposed data-eviction window & cross-border archive handling

Hi Sara / team,

Following our call last week I wanted to put a concrete proposal in writing so Legal and your team have something to react to. High-level summary:

- Backup eviction cadence: primary backups (hot-tier) retained for 30 days; warm backups retained for 90 days before eviction; cold/archival snapshots retained for 540 days but only accessible to support with approved legal request.
- Emergency purge SLA: when a valid data deletion request (DPA / customer instruction) is received, we aim to remove customer data from active indices and hot/warm backups within 48 hours, with a best-effort purge from cold/archival snapshots within 14 days depending on subprocessor timelines.
- Log retention: raw request logs are rotated at 90 days; aggregated usage logs can be retained up to 12 months on request (pseudonymized).
- Cross-border replication: EU primary data is replicated to EU regions. We propose a 30-day replication buffer for DR in the US region that is geo-restricted and encrypted; any cross-border replica will be subject to the same purge workflows and will not extend the canonical retention.
- Forensic/legal holds: when an active litigation or regulatory hold is invoked, we will freeze the relevant datasets and pause eviction of matching snapshots/backups. Holds require an internal legal ticket and an explicit start/end date.

I've attached an eviction_matrix.xlsx (stub) that maps object types, retention tiers, and purge windows, and a draft-dpa-amendment.docx for suggested language to add to section 6.2 (subprocessors / cross-border).

Questions for your team:
1) Are there any regulatory controls that would require longer retention for Helix-specific workloads (e.g., payer audits)?
2) Would Helix accept aggregated logs (60–365 days) instead of raw logs for troubleshooting/archive requests?
3) Any subprocessors we need to call out by name with separate contractual obligations?

Happy to discuss — proposing a quick sync tomorrow if that helps.

Thanks,
